summary.text: A planetary core is the innermost layer or layers of a planet, and it can be entirely liquid or, as in Earth, a mix of solid and liquid layers.
Cores cannot be reached by drilling and almost no samples come from them, so they are studied indirectly through seismology, mineral physics and planetary dynamics.
Earth's core is about 85% iron and 5% nickel, with lighter elements thought to make up the rest of its mass.

items.prompt: In 1797 Henry Cavendish found Earth's average density to be about 5.5 times that of water. What did people conclude from this?

options.label: Earth must be much denser inside
Earth must be mostly water inside
Earth is the same rock all the way down

items.explain: Cavendish's figure led to the accepted belief that Earth is much denser in its interior.

items.prompt: Which Solar System body has a core that takes up the biggest share of its radius?
items.explain: Core sizes range from about 20% of the radius for the Moon up to 85% for Mercury.

items.prompt: A probe finds that a rocky planet's moment of inertia is well below 0.4. What does that suggest?

options.label: The planet is hollow at its centre
Its mass is packed toward the centre
It spins faster than other planets
It has an unusually thick atmosphere

items.explain: A moment of inertia below 0.4 means the planet's density is concentrated in the centre, as with Mercury's 0.346.

items.prompt: Iron and nickel alone would leave Earth's outer core 5–10% heavier than it really is. What is thought to make up the difference?
items.explain: The weight deficit is put down to lighter, iron-soluble elements; sulfur may be about 1.9%, and silicon and oxygen make up the rest.

items.prompt: In the giant impact hypothesis, the Mars-sized body Theia struck the early Earth. Where did most of the iron from both bodies end up?
items.explain: During the impact, the majority of the iron from Theia and the Earth was incorporated into Earth's core.

items.prompt: Jupiter's core is tiny compared with Jupiter itself. How does its mass compare with the whole Earth?
items.explain: Gas giant cores are proportionally small, yet Jupiter's is 10–30 times heavier than Earth.

beats.title: Hearts No Drill Can Reach
beats.hook: Almost no samples come from any planet's core, yet we know the Moon's core has a radius of 300 km.

beats.prompt: Put these steps in uncovering Earth's core in the order they happened.

items.label: Wiechert proposes an iron core like iron meteorites
Oldham detects the core from seismic waves
Seismologists find the boundary between outer and inner core

beats.explain: Cavendish worked in 1797, Wiechert in 1898, Oldham in 1906, and the outer–inner core boundary was known by 1936.

beats.prompt: Match each body to how much of its radius its core takes up.
beats.explain: Core size relative to the whole body differs a lot from one world to another.

beats.prompt: Apollo missions left seismometers that recorded moonquakes. What did the data show about the Moon's core?
beats.explain: The Moon's iron core has a liquid outer layer making up 60% of the core's volume, around a solid inner core.

choices.label: The Moon has no core at all
choices.feedback: Tempting for a small world, but the data showed a 300 km core.

choices.label: A core that is entirely solid rock
choices.feedback: The core is iron, and its outer layer is liquid.

choices.label: An iron core, liquid outside and solid inside
A core that is entirely liquid
choices.feedback: Its outer layer is liquid, but there is a solid inner core.

beats.prompt: Sort each element by how Earth's core holds it.
beats.explain: Earth's core contains half the planet's vanadium and chromium but is depleted in germanium and gallium.

beats.idea: Planetary cores are studied indirectly, through density, seismic waves and spin measurements, and they vary widely in size.
